ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, officers, and persons exercising effective control must undergo mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Korea's own punitive sanction list administered by the Financial Intelligence Unit of Korea. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to politically exposed persons (PEPs) including heads of state, ministers, senior judicial officials, military leaders, heads of law enforcement, and executives of state-owned enterprises. Screening must be performed before incorporation, at bank account opening, and continuously. Adverse hits require rejection of the onboarding or immediate filing of a suspicious transaction report with the Financial Intelligence Unit. For a POD custom apparel e-commerce target whose payment rails are Stripe and PayPal, risk tiering is Low_Risk_Standard but sanctions screening remains mandatory and is not waived.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (Internet Registration System iROS) Commercial Name Clearance Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act, the legal name of a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) must be formed in Hangul including the mandatory suffix 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa). The name clearance portal requires the exact Hangul designation to be submitted for uniqueness screening. Any foreign-language brand name may be transliterated phonetically into Hangul and appended as a secondary trade name in the Articles of Association; however, the registered statutory name must be purely Hangul. The four-tier naming convention consists of (1) legal entity type suffix, (2) distinctive brand or trade key, (3) business activity descriptor identifying the POD/garment sector, and (4) optional geographic or identifying element. English names cannot replace the registered Hangul name for corporate filings and bank onboarding; the legal due diligence trail must reconcile the English trade name to its Hangul transliteration in all document packages.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection from the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office due to confusing similarity, prohibited terms, or incomplete transliteration, the applicant or its legal counsel must file a written administrative appeal with the competent District Court registry within 14 calendar days from the date of rejection. The appeal must state the proposed name, cite the specific reason for rejection, provide a legal comparison of previously registered or similar marks, and submit evidence of the applicant's legitimate business purpose. The District Court registry board will review the appeal and issue a decision within 21 business days. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may file an administrative litigation with the High Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act, and a further appeal to the Supreme Court is permitted. No extension of the name reservation window is available while an appeal is pending; a fresh name clearance search may be submitted immediately after final resolution.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korean law does not expressly ban a virtual office or commercial mailbox for statutory registration, but the National Tax Service and municipal tax authorities require a fixed place of business where books, records, and operational personnel can be inspected. For a print-on-demand retail company, Stripe and PayPal acquired by Korean partner banks will normally reject a pure virtual mailbox address on the ground of insufficient commercial substance. A serviced office in Seoul with actual work stations, signage, and lease evidence is strongly recommended; if a virtual address is used, the company must maintain a written service agreement, landlord consent, and a physical inventory manifest. The tax registry will otherwise allocate a higher risk score and refuse registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for site inspection: (i) presence of company signboard and distinguishing logo; (ii) actual production/fulfilment equipment or computer work stations showing POD activity; (iii) active power meter and internet subscription in the corporate name; (iv) lease agreement and management office consent; (v) stock of apparel samples or warehousing arrangements. The quantified risk of an unannounced inspection is approximately 22% for a bona fide serviced office in Seoul or Busan, 58% for a virtual office with no physical presence, and 80% or higher where the address is shared with multiple unrelated companies or appears as a mail forwarding service on public registry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sang-beop), Act No. 1000, as amended, especially Articles 288-317 on incorporation of a stock company (Chusik Hoesa), Article 318 on legal effectiveness upon registration, Article 317(3) on registration of incorporation, and the Commercial Registration Act, Articles 37-45 on registration procedure; registration and license tax is imposed under the Local Tax Act at 0.4 percent of paid-in capital plus a 20 percent education surtax, with the official numeric fee in this dossier calculated for an illustrative paid-in capital of KRW 10,000,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office, Registration Division, the District Court (Jiwon-beopso) of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation (Jangnip Deunggi Sinucheong) filed under Article 317(3) of the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Act, accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, and corporate minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law does not require a minimum statutory paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the full subscription price of each issued share must be paid in cash into a blocked deposit account at a domestic bank before incorporation registration, and the paid-in funds may not be withdrawn until the court has issued the certificate of incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION COMPANY: CHUSIK HOESA (STOCK CORPORATION) DATE: [●]. WHEREAS the Company was formed pursuant to Articles of Incorporation dated [●] and with the share capital and subscribed shares described in the Share Subscription Schedule approved by the incorporators; and WHEREAS under Articles 316 and 317 of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, the Board of Directors must adopt resolutions to increase, perfect, and record the capital and statutory structure of the Company; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS THAT: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The Share Subscription Schedule dated [●] is hereby ratified and adopted, and the total subscription price for the issued shares, in the amount of [●] Korean won, is accepted as fully paid into the blocked capital deposit account at [●] Bank. The certificate of paid-in capital deposit issued by such bank is accepted as proof of payment, and the Company's paid-in capital shall be recorded as [●] Korean won, divided into [●] common shares with a par value of KRW [●] per share. 2. Banking Authorization. The principal banking relationship of the Company shall be established with [●] Bank, [●] Branch. The Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [●], together with any additional director designated by the Representative Director, are hereby authorized to open corporate accounts, execute all bank account forms and online banking mandates, issue payment instructions, sign deposit and securities documents, and amend account signatory lists as necessary for the Company's ordinary business. 3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at [●], Republic of Korea, and the Representative Director is authorized to sign the lease, obtain the consent of the building owner, pay deposits and rent, and register the address with the court registration office and tax authorities. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. [●] is hereby appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer; [●] is appointed Director; and [●] is appointed Auditor, each to serve until the first ordinary general meeting of shareholders and to exercise all powers vested by the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. 5. Further Acts. Any one director or officer is authorized to prepare, execute, notarize, and file all applications, declarations, powers of attorney, and legal documents, and to pay all fees necessary to register the Company, open bank accounts, appoint accountants, and commence e-commerce operations. This Resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Sign, and Notarize Korean-Language Articles of Incorporation and File Foreign Investment Report if Applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public under the Korean Notary Act; where foreign investment is involved, KOTRA (Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency) or a domestic foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating shareholders must prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language containing the corporate name with the Chusik Hoesa suffix, the purpose clause limited to e-commerce and print-on-demand custom apparel retailing, registered office address, authorized and issued share amounts, class and par value of shares, appointment method for directors, auditor provisions, publication method, and fiscal year. Each incorporator must sign and seal the draft before a Korean notary public, who verifies identities, legal capacity, and the lawfulness of the business purpose. If any non-resident shareholder invests KRW 100,000,000 or more, an ex ante foreign investment report must be completed through KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank; a voluntary report below that amount is recommended for future capital protection. The notarized Articles must match the registration application exactly to avoid court queries.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean signed and sealed by each incorporator
Valid passport or national identity card of each incorporator, with a Korean notarized translation if required
Certified proof of address and nationality for each non-resident shareholder
Foreign Investment Report application or receipt, if applicable
Power of attorney and identity document of the attorney, if signing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to the purpose clause or corporate name, amend the Articles and re-notarize before proceeding. If KOTRA or the bank flags a missing foreign-investment document, supplement the filing within five business days and re-submit through the same electronic portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Blocked Share-Capital Deposit Account and Make Full Payment of the Subscription Price
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank authorized to operate in the Republic of Korea that accepts incorporation share subscriptions; for cross-border remittances, a foreign exchange bank applying the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the incorporators must open an incorporation deposit account in the name of the Company with a Korean bank. Each subscriber must pay in full the subscription price for the shares subscribed before registration, and the payment cannot be offset by any receivable or other claim. For foreign residents, the remittance must be made through a foreign exchange bank and evidenced by an inward remittance certificate. The bank will verify the subscription schedule and issue the Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit required by Article 317 of the Commercial Act, specifying the depositor, deposit amount, account number, and escrowed status. The escrowed funds may not be withdrawn until the official certificate of incorporation registration is presented to the bank.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
List of subscribers and share subscription schedule
Certificate of foreign investment report, if applicable
Company account application form used by the designated bank
Identity documents and power of attorney for any authorized signatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening because of a name mismatch or incomplete subscription schedule, obtain a corrected subscriber list or amended Articles and resubmit. If the capital deposit certificate is inaccurate, return it to the bank for correction; do not proceed with registration until the certificate is exact.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene Organizational Meeting, Inspect Paid-in Capital, and Elect Initial Directors and Auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and share subscribers acting in the statutory organizational meeting under Commercial Act Articles 294-310; the newly elected directors then convene the first board meeting to appoint the Representative Director
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All share subscribers must hold a statutory organizational meeting to inspect the capital deposit certificate and confirm that the full subscription price has been paid. During this meeting, the subscribers elect the initial board of directors and, if required by the Articles, the statutory auditor. The newly elected directors then hold the first board meeting, approve the election of a Representative Director, and appoint any required statutory auditor. The minutes of both meetings must be prepared, signed or sealed by the chairman and attendees, and preserved as corporate records. Capital inspection and appointment decisions must comply with the quorum and voting rules in the Commercial Act and the Articles. For a one-person company, a written resolution signed by the sole shareholder and sole appointed director may replace the formal meeting, provided it contains the same inspection, election, and appointment outcomes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit
Notice of organizational meeting and record of attendance or waiver
Minutes of the organizational meeting
Minutes of the first board meeting appointing the Representative Director
Written consent of each elected director to accept office
Written consent of the elected auditor to accept office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the required quorum is not present, issue a revised notice and hold a postponed meeting. If an elected director declines appointment, pass a replacement board resolution and obtain a new written consent, then correct the minutes before any court filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation to the District Court Commercial Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office, Registration Division, of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office, such as the Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registration Office in Seoul
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the payment of capital and the organizational meetings are complete, the applicant must submit the statutory registration application to the court registrar. The application must present the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, organizational meeting minutes, first board meeting minutes, written acceptances of directors and auditor, signed specimen of the Representative Director's signature and seal, proof of registration tax and education tax payment, and evidence of the registered office. The registrar verifies statutory compliance, checks that the corporate name and purpose are lawful, confirms that the paid-in capital is fully deposited, and ensures that the registered office is within the court's jurisdiction. Once accepted, the court enters the Company in the commercial register and issues the official corporate registration certificate, which releases the escrowed capital upon presentation to the bank.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation filed on the court form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Paid-in Capital Deposit
Minutes of the organizational meeting and the first board meeting
Written consents of directors and auditor
Identity documents and specimen signature of the Representative Director
Payment receipt for registration tax and education tax
Consent of building owner or office lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order, respond in writing within the fixed deadline, normally two weeks, with the requested documents or corrected text. If the application is rejected, cure the specific defect and re-file, or file an immediate appeal under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within the permitted appellate period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Registration Certificate and File the E-Commerce Telecommunications Sales Business Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office for business registration; the local Si/Gun/Gu government office for the communication sales business report under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receiving the certified corporate registration certificate, the Company must complete all operational registrations. First, the Company must file a business registration application with the District Tax Office under the Value-Added Tax Act, describing its business as online retail of print-on-demand custom apparel, and obtain the Business Registration Certificate. Second, because sales are made through an internet shopping channel, the Company must file the Telecommunications Sales Business Report with the local Si/Gun/Gu office, including the trade name, representative, address, customer service contact, after-sales policy, and online shopping mall address. Third, if personal information is processed, including data obtained through Stripe, PayPal, or the online store, the Company must comply with the Personal Information Protection Act and install a privacy officer or privacy processing registration as required. These completed filings allow the corporate bank account and payment gateway to operate lawfully.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration issued by the court
Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution confirming the registered office
Lease contract or letter of consent for the registered office
Utility bill or occupancy proof for the registered office
Representative Director's identity card
Online store URL and electronic commerce terms if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office or local government requests additional information, submit the supplementary documents through the National Tax Service HomeTax system or the local administrative e-government portal and retain the electronic receipt. If the report is rejected because of an incorrect business type, correct the business purpose and re-file via the same authority within the same business day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The Company's primary ISIC 4791 business is online retail and print-on-demand custom merchandise retailing, not physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing. For general e-commerce regulatory guidance, the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and the Fair Trade Commission of Korea are the relevant advisory and enforcement authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No industrial operating license is required because the Company does not fall under ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx, or 52xx physical operations. The Company must still hold a Business Registration Certificate issued by the National Tax Service and file the Telecommunications Sales Business Report with the local Si/Gun/Gu office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea (MoE) and its regional environmental offices
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. No Environmental Impact Assessment category is triggered by online retailing of print-on-demand custom apparel. If the Company later owns or operates a physical printing, dyeing, assembly, or warehousing facility, the project will be screened under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, and a Full EIA, preliminary review, or environmental registration may be required depending on facility size and location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. The Company currently has no industrial wastewater, exhaust, or hazardous waste discharge points. If the Company later operates garment-printing or chemical-handling equipment, it must comply with the Water Environment Conservation Act effluent standards, the Clean Air Conservation Act air pollutant and volatile organic compound limits, and the Waste Management Act manifest system, with facility-specific numeric limits to be fixed in the environmental permit issued by the local environmental authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the current pure online retail office model. No Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace safety license is required for a standard corporate office. If the Company later operates its own warehouse, distribution center, print shop, or chemical storage area, it must obtain a Fire Safety Certificate and the applicable Fire Protection Inspection approval from the National Fire Agency under the Fire Fighting Systems Act, a structural safety inspection for the premises, and an occupational safety and health clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Until such physical operations are added, the building owner's general fire safety certificate is sufficient for the leased office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax System (http://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must appoint a domestic tax representative in Korea before commencing any taxable supply or business. Submit an application for business registration (business registration certificate) to the competent district tax office through the HomeTax system, attaching the entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of association, board resolution appointing the domestic tax representative, power of attorney, evidence of registered place of business in Korea, and passport or certificate of incorporation of the foreign entity. The NTS issues a 10-digit tax identification number (also used as the VAT registration number) upon approval. If the foreign entity has no physical presence but makes electronic supplies of services or sells goods through a domestic fulfillment arrangement, it must still register through the same non-resident business registration procedure for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korea does not operate check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections for a Chusik Hoesa. A limited group consolidation election exists under the Corporate Tax Act for qualifying domestic subsidiaries, but it does not alter the entity-level tax classification of the standalone entity and is not an indirect tax election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for corporations; every Chusik Hoesa engaging in taxable supplies in Korea is mandatorily required to register for VAT. A simplified taxable person threshold of KRW 30,000,000 per year applies only to individual entrepreneurs, not to a stock corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) issuance and real-time transmission to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax system for all business-to-business and any invoice-issuing supplies. Corporate taxpayers are obliged to issue electronic tax invoices to all registered buyers within the statutory timeframe. The system uses an XML-based API and electronic medium for direct submission, with a one-day transmission window after issuance for normal cases. Cash receipts must also be issued and reported for qualifying business-to-consumer cash sales. There is no separate anti-fraud digital stamping or pre-approval per invoice, but the NTS operates real-time VAT return matching and compulsory e-invoice auditing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported outside the customs territory of Korea qualify for the 0% VAT rate under the Value-Added Tax Act. The statutory criteria require actual exportation of the goods, transfer of title to a foreign buyer, physical shipment of the goods from Korea under customs control, and timely receipt of the export proceeds in foreign currency. For print-on-demand retail, the goods must be manufactured and shipped from Korea directly to the overseas customer with documentation proving that the goods left the Korean customs territory and were delivered outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate issued by Korea Customs Service)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Korea
Proof of foreign exchange receipt, including the Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate and the equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)
Order/purchase confirmation from the overseas buyer and marketplace sales records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may disallow export zero-rating if the required customs declaration, transport documents, or foreign exchange receipts are missing, incomplete, or inconsistent. If zero-rating is denied, the unpaid VAT of 10% becomes immediately collectible, plus statutory late-payment surcharges and understatement penalties. Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, negligent underreporting attracts a penalty of up to 10% of the unpaid tax, fraudulent underreporting attracts a penalty of up to 40%, and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may impose criminal sanctions for falsely substantiated export claims. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days may also result in loss of the zero-rating benefit and separate penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (The Central Bank of the Republic of Korea) and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN), operating under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely open capital and current account under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Korean won (KRW) being fully convertible for current account transactions including trade in goods, services, royalties, and dividends. However, capital account transactions remain subject to a formal reporting and licensing regime, primarily through the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN) and designated foreign exchange banks. Exporters are generally required to receive export proceeds within a defined statutory period, but the mandatory surrender requirement has been substantially liberalized; since 1995, export proceeds may be held in foreign currency accounts without forced conversion, although a reporting obligation remains for settlement. Profit remittance, dividends, and capital repatriation for foreign investors are permissible but require underlying certification of inward foreign investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and Korean banks mandate a tax clearance certificate and capital verification for outward remittances above specific thresholds. There are no blanket conversion prohibitions, but foreign exchange transactions may be subject to criminal penalty for misrepresentation of purpose codes. Businesses engaged in cross-border trade, such as the target Print-on-Demand custom apparel retail enterprise, must ensure precise classification of payments between current and capital accounts, use designated licensed banks for inward remittance to avoid delays, and be prepared to submit transaction documentation to the bank's compliance division to satisfy the Foreign Exchange Information Network reporting requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected and settled within five years from the date of export declaration, provided the export contract or payment terms do not specify a shorter period. For proceeds received in foreign currency, the exporting entity may retain the funds in a foreign currency account at a domestic licensed bank without mandatory conversion into KRW. If conversion to KRW is performed, it must be executed through a foreign exchange bank, and a Foreign Exchange Settlement Notice is required for amounts exceeding the equivalent of 5,000 USD per transaction. Any diversion, delayed receipt, or non-receipt of export proceeds beyond the statutory timeline must be reported to the Ministry of Economy and Finance with a justification, and failure to do so may result in administrative sanctions or criminal liability.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) are generally not viable as primary banking rails in South Korea. The Korean financial regulatory system requires any entity engaging in domestic payment services, foreign exchange brokerage, or cross-border remittance to obtain a license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or be classified as a 'Foreign Exchange Business Operator' registered with the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Non-bank EMIs domiciled in jurisdictions such as the UK, Singapore, or Europe are not automatically passportable into Korea and cannot compete with domestic licensed foreign exchange banks for inward investor capital, export proceeds collection, or dividend remittance clearing. They may serve as secondary platforms for merchant acquiring through Stripe or PayPal if those entities partner with domestic banks, but the corporate entity must maintain a primary domestic KRW settlement account at a Tier-1 commercial bank. Any proposal to route capital injections or trade disbursements exclusively through an offshore EMI would trigger strong AML and foreign exchange non-compliance findings during bank onboarding, and is expressly discouraged.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean banks require a physical presence for the statutory representative (CEO or Director) or a full legal proxy through a notarized power of attorney apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Remote or consular proxy opening is not permitted in the absence of a direct banking relationship; even when a domestic proxy is designated, the bank's compliance team will demand CCTV-verified signature matching and original corporate chop, plus certified copies of the board resolution authorizing the account. In practice, at least one director with signing authority must attend a face-to-face onboarding interview at a bank branch or via an in-person visit from a bank official, unless the bank accepts a biometric-verified remote video process under the Financial Supervisory Service's simplified electronic KYC guidelines (Act on Enforcement of the Financial Transactions in Electronic Form). The safe and preferred path is for the authorized Korean director to appear physically in-branch for the initial account opening and again for foreign-exchange dealer registration, as this sharply reduces the probability of rejection or extended compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FATCA and common reporting standard (CRS) beneficial ownership opacity due to multi-tier foreign holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An exhaustive corporate chain ownership diagram showing every intermediate entity to the ultimate natural person, all passports, foreign investor registration certificate, signed W-8BEN/E and CRS self-certification forms, plus certified board resolutions from each holding entity confirming no undisclosed nominees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of wealth or source of funds for initial capital escrow deposit exceeding KRW 100 million from a non-bank offshore emitter
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the remitting parties for the preceding 12 months, audited financial statements of the overseas shareholder, signed declaration of source of funds, tax payment certificates of the ultimate beneficial owner, and legal documentation evidencing the commercial reason for the capital injection (e.g., subscription agreement, M&A contract, or working capital funding facility).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential mismatch between declared business scope (Print-on-Demand retail) and anticipated high-frequency cross-border payments for custom merchandise manufacturing and logistics
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements with print-on-demand fulfillment partners and raw material suppliers, customs clearance and export/import declarations for the past three transaction cycles, logistics bills of lading, e-commerce sales platform contracts (Amazon, Shopify, Cafe24), and a 12-month cash flow forecast showing the expected currency conversion pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Designation or sanctions screening hits arising from overseas clients or payment intermediaries due to the low-risk retail apparel sector but high data asymmetry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full due diligence files on every downstream buyer and payment facilitator, including corporate registry extracts, OECD country of residence proof, negative press review, clean sanctions screening results from OFAC, UN, EU, and Korean Foreign Ministry lists, and a written commitment to maintain a 'no hidden beneficial ownership' covenant in each commercial contract.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment (FDI) into the Korean Chusik Hoesa must be routed through a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank via SWIFT MT103 in USD, EUR, or KRW, with the wire designated as 'Capital Injection for Foreigner Investment' and the Inward Investment Code 'FOIC' captured in the SWIFT field 70. The bank will require a Certificate of Foreign Investment Notification issued by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or the Foreign Exchange Bank after the investment filing. Within 30 days of receipt, a Foreign Exchange Settlement Notice must be submitted if the amount exceeds KRW 5,000,000, and the receiving bank will perform capital verification and issue a Certificate of Capital Injection, which is then used for the registration of the foreign-owned company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Any inbound remittance not covered by a corresponding investment declaration will be automatically classified as non-declared foreign exchange receipt and may be refused or suspended.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements involving payment to international garment manufacturers or POD production facilities, the Korean entity should use SWIFT MT103 single-payment transfers for standard supplier invoices, or Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) confirmed by a Korean Tier-1 bank when the counterparty demands documentary security. Documentary Collections are also permissible for lower-value transactions. Each outbound remittance must be accompanied by the Foreign Exchange Purpose Code (e.g., 'A1000' for trade in goods, 'A5230' for business services), the underlying commercial invoice, a transport document (e.g., air waybill, bill of lading), and where applicable, the Customs export declaration. Amounts exceeding USD 50,000 are subject to documentary review, and the bank may require submission of the original export contract or proforma invoice. Hedging is limited to plain-vanilla products offered by licensed banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward exchange contracts (plain vanilla) with a maturity up to 12 months, requiring an underlying real export/import trade transaction and confirmation of anticipated FX cash flows from the bank's foreign exchange dealer.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permitted only for non-trade-related capital transactions and for foreign investors hedging their investment positions in Korean won instruments, but are not permissible for a domestic Chusik Hoesa entity's apparel trade payables; domestic trade collectives should instead use onshore forwards.

Currency swap boundaries restrict Korean resident companies to simple cross-currency swaps with a licensed bank for hedging investment capital or large procurement contracts, provided such swaps are registered with the Bank of Korea and have clear cash-flow matching documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and financial statement approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external regulator; AGM minutes and adopted financial statements retained at the registered office and available to shareholders, the National Tax Service and the Commercial Act enforcement authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end; for a calendar-year company not later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM or retain minutes may expose each responsible director to an administrative fine under the Korean Commercial Act; non-approved financial statements may not be distributed and protracted non-compliance may result in court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return with tax reconciliation schedules and audited or reviewed financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the fiscal year end; the statutory filing period is three months from fiscal year end for calendar-year corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 20% unfaithful-return additional tax is imposed on the understated or unpaid corporate income tax, plus late-payment surcharge on unpaid tax; chronic non-filing triggers a NTS forced assessment, seizure of bank and trade assets, enforcement of the statutory tax lien, and criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax (local surcharge) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial or Metropolitan City Government through the local income tax collection office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 following the fiscal year end for calendar-year companies; within four months of fiscal year end for non-calendar fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay the local corporate income tax exposes the company to local-tax additional dues, a 20% unfaithful-return penalty in serious cases, daily late-payment interest and compulsory collection by the local government.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) or KOTRA through the designated foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following the fiscal year end; the anniversary report is due within three months of fiscal year end for each foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing can result in administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, loss of foreign-invested tax incentives, and adverse findings in banking and FDI reviews; there is no administrative strike-off but the company may lose foreign-investment status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 25 of the same tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-declared VAT attracts a 10% negligence penalty on the unpaid VAT amount, plus daily late-payment surcharge; persistent delinquency leads to tax seizure and blocking of the tax clearance certificate needed for bank finance and government contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before July 25 of the same tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-declared VAT attracts a 10% negligence penalty on the unpaid VAT amount, plus daily late-payment surcharge; persistent delinquency leads to tax seizure and blocking of the tax clearance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before October 25 of the same tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-declared VAT attracts a 10% negligence penalty on the unpaid VAT amount, plus daily late-payment surcharge; persistent delinquency leads to tax seizure and blocking of the tax clearance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 25 of the following tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-declared VAT attracts a 10% negligence penalty on the unpaid VAT amount, plus daily late-payment surcharge; persistent delinquency leads to tax seizure and blocking of the tax clearance certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements filing on DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) through the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) DART system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held by March 31 for calendar-year companies and the audited audit report and audited financial statements must be filed with FSC through DART within 14 days after the AGM; in any event not later than 6 months after fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or file the audit report is punishable by administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 and liability of the representative director; the FSC may order corrective measures and, for repeated violations, require the removal of directors or apply for a court-ordered dissolution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa must obtain an independent certified CPA audit if (i) its total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approx. USD 8.9 million at KRW 1,350/USD), (ii) it is listed on a Korean stock exchange or is a financial-industry company, or (iii) it is specifically designated by the Financial Services Commission. Revenue and headcount are not independent statutory audit triggers under Korea's external audit regime; a print-on-demand retail company below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold will be exempt from mandatory external audit unless it has listed or financial-industry status, but it must still keep tax-compliant accounting records and corporate books.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; non-listed SMEs may instead apply the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for Small and Medium Entities (K-GAAP or SME GAAP) when not required to use K-IFRS. Tax reporting additionally requires the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act reconciliation schedules and the Principal Tax Return and supplementary documents required by the National Tax Service.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not maintain a public UBO annual declaration for all private stock corporations. A Chusik Hoesa must keep an accurate shareholders register at its registered office, and a share transfer has company-law effect only when the transferee is entered in the register; for foreign shareholders, any acquisition or disposal that creates, changes, or terminates foreign-invested enterprise status must be reported to MOTIE or the designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days, and the annual foreign-invested enterprise operation report is due by March 31 each year. The company must also retain underlying ownership documents for AML and CRS/AEOI identification, but no annual UBO fee or register filing is made to a Korean companies registry.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,500 per year for a registered office, mail forwarding, and corporate secretarial retainer in Korea; full bookkeeping, VAT and CIT filing and annual maintenance services generally range from USD 2,000 - USD 6,000 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No mandatory audit cost is incurred below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold; if the audit threshold is met or a voluntary audit is required by creditors or investors, a small or mid-size print-on-demand retail corporation can expect a certified audit fee ranging from USD 8,000 - USD 25,000, with larger K-IFRS audits exceeding USD 30,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 21% national Corporate Income Tax (CIT) on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion, with mandatory 10% local income tax surcharge producing a combined top effective headline rate of 23.1%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory progressive CIT rates are 9% for tax base up to KRW 200 million, 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, and 21% for tax base over KRW 20 billion, plus the 10% local surcharge. Eligible incentives include the Special Tax Reduction Control Act R&D expense tax credit (up to 30% of qualified R&D costs, 40% for new-growth technologies), SME tax deduction, foreign-investment-zone tax holidays (100% exemption for the first 3 to 5 years, 50% reduction for 2 following years), Free Economic Zone / Free Trade Zone preferential regimes for export-oriented digital commerce entities, and tax-deferral for corporate restructuring and capital gains reinvestment. A POD apparel retailing corporation may claim the small/Middle business income deduction and income exemptions for foreign-invested companies if it maintains substantive local employment and IT infrastructure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system; quarterly prepayment returns (법인세 중간예납) are filed in the intermediate period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayment of CIT applies where estimated taxable income for the current fiscal year exceeds certain statutory thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 3 months of the fiscal year-end (by March 31 for a December 31 year-end). The tax amount must be paid by the same deadline; an extension of up to 1 month is available for qualified conventional requests, and an additional 1-month extension may be granted for international filing groups subject to cross-border disclosure requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total domestic and export sales from print-on-demand custom apparel retailing, including amounts derived from Stripe, PayPal, and other cross-border payment gateways, grossed up by location-of-rendering rules under the VAT Act and CIT rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross sales in KRW after mandatory customs and remittance data reconciliation. Export sales to foreign consumers may be zero-rated for VAT but must still be included in CIT revenue. Attach a schedule reconciling e-commerce platform net settlements to gross sales; otherwise the tax office may impute additional revenue under the omniscient data matching program.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of procuring blank apparel, printing inks, sublimation films, packaging, freight-in, warehouse rents, and third-party POD platform fees recognized as COGS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduction is allowed to the extent attributable to generating taxable income. Intercompany COGS paid to related foreign printers or raw-material suppliers must be priced at arm's length under the Korean Transfer Pricing Act and supported by a Local File if cross-border related-party transactions exceed the statutory threshold. Failure to substantiate the business purpose of offshore POD vendors may trigger a deemed-disallowance and TP adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as Box 1 less Box 2, reported before operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A disproportionately low gross profit margin relative to OECD apparel e-commerce comparables will attract transfer-pricing scrutiny; the taxpayer should maintain monthly gross-margin reconciliations, benchmark studies, and platform fee allocations between distribution channel and market functions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 — Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing commissions, advertising, salaries, IT infrastructure, payment processing fees, bad debts, royalties, management fees, and professional services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign affiliates for marketing, management, and technical support are deductible only if the sign-off documents, actual service delivery logs, and headcount-support evidence are retained. Invoices routed through low-tax jurisdictions without economic substance in the State of residence will be denied as a constructive dividend; the payor must also withhold 22% on taxable Korean-source service fees and may be required to file an International Transaction (TP) Report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit or loss computed as gross profit less SG&A, adjusted for corporate tax book-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For loss-makers, Korean tax authorities apply substance-over-form rules and may add back payments to related foreign entities lacking resident personnel, premises, or business risk. If operating loss is used to offset future taxable income, the 10-year carryforward limitation is applied; the entity must keep immutable accounting records and e-document logs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 — Non-Operating Income and Non-Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, FX gains and losses, dividend income, gains on asset disposals, and non-operating write-offs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest expenses paid on intercompany loans from non-resident shareholders are subject to thin-capitalization and hidden thin-capitalization rules under the Korean International Tax Adjustment Act. Where the loan capital exceeds 3 times (6 times for financial institutions) the investee's capital, the deemed interest portion is non-deductible. Also disclose all foreign bank accounts and 1099-like financial account schedules required under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance leverage; penalties apply for omission of foreign income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 — Taxable Income Adjustments and Tax Base Determination
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income is reconciled to taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses, subtracting exempt income (foreign-free-zone income, foreign direct investment tax holidays, IP box benefits, research and development investments), and applying tax loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders with a Korean Chusik Hoesa must file an accurate profit-participation declaration and beneficial ownership schedule. Any re-invoicing or pricing manipulation of POD custom-apparel transactions through related foreign affiliates will cause a transfer-pricing adjustment under the arm's-length standard. Tax-exempt FIZ income must be isolated in the books; commingling with domestic POD retail revenue destroys the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 — Final Tax Computation, Withholding, and Settlement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT liability computed with progressive rates plus 10% local income tax surcharge, reduced by intermediate prepayments, foreign tax credits, and tax credits for independent work.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the company distributes profits to a non-resident shareholder, 22% dividend withholding is statutorily due on the gross amount unless the shareholder supplies a valid Tax Residency Certificate and applies for treaty relief. The tax office will not allow treaty-exemption unless the beneficial ownership declaration and no-PE certificate are filed before the distribution. Directors must sign the digital tax filing; deliberate embezzlement or false statement may trigger the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 20% of the underreported tax for negligent understatement, 40% for grossly negligent or intentional understatement, and 10% to 20% for unfaithful withholding; unpaid tax accrues daily late-payment interest of 0.022% (approximately 8.03% per annum) until settled. Failure to submit a corporate tax return at all subjects the taxpayer to administrative fine of up to 1% of turnover and, where tax unpaid exceeds KRW 50 million, criminal referral under the Framework Act on National Taxes and Punishment of Tax Evaders Act (imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to KRW 500 million). Incorrect or misleading TP documentation may attract a separate penalty of up to KRW 30 million and up to 30% of the transfer-pricing adjustment amount.
